claims.text: Adding approximately 7 at.% Zr to Ti65(AlCrNbV)35 and applying thermomechanical processing will increase high-temperature yield strength by roughly 20–30%.
The Zr-modified alloy will retain room-temperature ductility comparable to the Zr-free baseline.
The Zr modification will slightly decrease the alloy density relative to Ti65(AlCrNbV)35.
The baseline Ti65(AlCrNbV)35 alloy has a single-phase BCC structure in the conventionally cast state.
A processing route combining 50% hot rolling, 70% cold rolling, and rapid annealing has previously been applied to the Ti65(AlCrNbV)35-xZrx alloy family.
Rapid annealing at approximately 850 °C with a heating rate near 15 K/s and a duration of 30–50 s is an appropriate treatment for the proposed alloy.
The predicted strength advantage should hold under quasi-static loading from 850 to 1150 °C.
Adding Zr increases the atomic-size difference in Ti65(AlCrNbV)35-xZrx alloys.
The increased atomic-size difference enhances substitutional solid-solution strengthening.
The Zr addition and thermomechanical process produce a refined, homogeneous microstructure with uniformly distributed grain sizes.
Zr has a larger atomic radius than Ti and therefore produces lattice distortion that impedes dislocation motion.
Zr-induced lattice distortion impedes dislocation motion particularly at high temperatures.
Grain refinement from the thermomechanical process improves elevated-temperature yield strength.
The lower intrinsic density of Zr is responsible for reducing the overall alloy density.
A fine, homogeneous microstructure preserves good room-temperature ductility.
Zr-containing Ti65(AlCrNbV)35-xZrx alloys have densities of approximately 5 g/cm3.
As-cast Zr-containing alloys in this series can exhibit tensile yield strength above 1000 MPa and tensile ductility of at least 20%.
Prior literature supports improved high-temperature properties from Zr addition in similar alloys.

contradictions.description: The headline hypothesis describes hot rolling followed by rapid annealing, whereas the intervention and conditions insert a 70% cold-rolling step between hot rolling and annealing.
